title: Microsoft Stock (MSFT) Falls 0.2% to $530.14 (Oct 29)
summary: Microsoft (MSFT) closed at $530.14 on Oct 29, down 0.16%, giving up early gains after its Azure-led earnings beat as Alphabet's slide hit the Nasdaq.
body_markdown:
The move was milder than the broader tech selloff. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.38% to 26,184.72, the S&P 500 slipped 0.30% to 7,720.39 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.25% to 52,342.56, leaving Microsoft 1.22 percentage points ahead of the Nasdaq. Among large tech peers,[Alphabet (GOOGL)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/googl/) dropped 12.64% and[Amazon (AMZN)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/amzn/) fell 4.25%, while[Meta Platforms (META)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/meta/) rose 1.96%. The US 10-year Treasury yield closed at 4.99%, down 5.6 basis points.


Near its 52-week high. Microsoft closed 3.81% below its 52-week high of $551.15 and 51.82% above its 52-week low of $349.20.


## Why Microsoft Stock Fell


None of the reports reviewed name a Microsoft-specific reason for the 0.16% decline; financial media described a stock that gave back its gains while the wider tech sector sold off.


Microsoft released its[fiscal first-quarter results](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/microsoft-cloud-beat-backs-rebound-lower-capex-hits-coreweave-and-neocloud-stocks-msft-crwv/) after the close on Wednesday, October 28. According to the[company's official release](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/earnings/fy-2027-q1/press-release-webcast) , revenue rose 19% to $92.3 billion, Azure revenue rose 48% to $33.2 billion and Microsoft Cloud revenue rose 30% to $63.9 billion. Operating income grew 21% to $45.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share rose 32% to $4.92 ($4.89 on a non-GAAP basis, up 18%).


On Thursday, investors treated the two cloud giants differently. As reported by Investing.com,[Alphabet's post-earnings slide](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/alphabet-q3-earnings-miss-sinks-stock-reignites-ai-capex-fears-googl-nasdaq-futures/) weighed on the AI trade, while Microsoft's Azure unit helped it to a top- and bottom-line beat. Per[Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/article/why-microsoft-stock-isnt-getting-crushed-like-google-stock-after-its-earnings-report-092500217.html) , Azure growth came in about 300 basis points above analyst estimates and capital expenditure was about $5 billion below estimates. The same report said investors sensitive to negative free cash flow across Big Tech hit Alphabet harder, because Microsoft kept positive cash flow.


After the close,[Barron's](https://finance.yahoo.com/m/b19c6e1a-ed1d-3f04-8a85-fb91af9a3ec9/microsoft-issues-%2425-billion.html) reported that Microsoft issued $25 billion in new bonds, adding to a wave of borrowing by large tech companies to fund AI spending.


## MSFT Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Azure outlook: Microsoft guided Azure growth of 49% to 50% in constant currency for the current quarter, according to Investing.com, a range Yahoo Finance said was about four points above consensus.
- Cloud scale: Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $63.9 billion in the quarter, up 30%, according to the company.


### Risks


- Heavy AI spending: capital expenditure was $45.2 billion in the quarter, up about 30% from a year earlier, as Microsoft builds data center infrastructure to meet AI demand, according to[CIO Dive](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/microsoft-google-report-booming-ai-204117062.html) .
- Rising borrowing: Barron's said the $25 billion bond issue adds to an AI debt spree among large tech companies.
- Focus on AI returns: Investing.com reported that worries about returns on AI spending weighed on tech on Thursday.
- Consumer weakness: revenue in the Devices and Consumer segment fell 3% to $15.5 billion, per the company's release.
